args.title: Check rollup send time more often than once an hour
args.body:
File: src/notifications/rollup.ts

startRollupSchedule only ticks at the top of each UTC hour, so isRollupDue (which compares the user's local hour to SEND_HOUR) is only ever evaluated when the UTC clock is exactly on the hour. For users whose zone has a non-zero-minute UTC offset (Asia/Kolkata +5:30, America/St_Johns -3:30, Asia/Kathmandu +5:45), local 08:00 falls partway through a UTC hour, so the first tick where their local hour reads 8 is already 08:30 or 08:45 local, not 08:00. Ticking every minute (or every 15 minutes) instead of every hour, and/or having isRollupDue also check that the local minute is 0, would let these users receive the rollup at the correct local time.

label: bug
file: src/notifications/rollup.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

The rollup scheduler only ticks at the top of each UTC hour (`startRollupSchedule`'s `setInterval(tick, HOUR_MS)`), and `isRollupDue` fires on the first tick whose local hour (via `localHour`) equals `SEND_HOUR`. For zones whose UTC offset includes minutes — Asia/Kolkata (+5:30), America/St_Johns (-3:30), Asia/Kathmandu (+5:45) — local 08:00 falls in the middle of a UTC hour, so the first hourly tick that reads local hour 8 is already 08:30 or 08:45. Whole-hour zones (London, Chicago) happen to line up with the UTC hour boundary and so get it at exactly 08:00. Ticking more often (e.g. every minute) and/or checking the local minute as well as the hour would fix this for all offsets.
